## Text & Documents

### Word Counter
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/word-counter
- What: Count words, characters & reading time
- FAQ:
  - Does the word counter store my text?
    - Answer: No. Word, character and sentence counting runs entirely on your device with no upload; e.g. an 800-word draft or 5,000 characters stays on-device, works offline free, and closing the tab clears text. Nothing is sent to a server.
  - How is reading time calculated?
    - Answer: It divides word count by average reading speed of 200 to 238 words per minute. Example: 800 words at 200 WPM is 4.0 minutes and at 238 WPM is 3.4 minutes; 1,500 words is 6.3-7.5 minutes. Skim readers finish faster, technical readers slower.
  - What text size can it handle?
  - What length should different content types target?
  - Why do Word and Google Docs show slightly different counts?
- Steps: Paste your essay draft (Paste a 1,500-word essay draft or 800-word blog post into the large input box for instant counting.) → Watch live totals update (Watch live totals for words, characters with spaces, sentences, paragraphs, and estimated reading minutes update.) → Check time, ease and density → Trim to intent then copy

- URL: https://tool4saas.com/case-converter
- What: UPPER, lower, Title, camel & more
- FAQ:
  - Which text cases are supported?
    - Answer: Supports UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Sentence case, camelCase, plus snake_case for diverse workflows. For example, hello world example transforms to HELLO WORLD, Hello World Example, helloWorldExample, plus hello_world_example instantly. Select one-click options for headings, identifiers, plus titles and documentation labels consistently.
  - Does it change my numbers or punctuation?
    - Answer: Transforms alphabetic characters while preserving digits, punctuation, emojis, plus spacing integrity. For example, hello world 123! retains numerals while letters shift. Camel plus snake variants strip spaces systematically; previews reveal outcomes plus copy affordances immediately for codebases headings plus statistical labels.
  - How does Title Case handle small words?
  - Is my pasted text uploaded to a server?
  - Why do developers and students reuse conversions?
- Steps: Paste text (Enter sample hello world example or longer paragraph requiring uniform stylistic treatment for headings plus identifiers.) → Pick a case (Select UPPER, lower, Title, Sentence, camelCase, or snake_case matching destination conventions for code documentation plus publishing.) → Preview result → Copy output

### Readability Checker
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/readability-checker
- What: Flesch & grade level
- FAQ:
  - What does Flesch Ease signify?
    - Answer: Scale 0 to 100 where higher denotes simpler prose; 60-70 suits plain articles while 90-100 fits very easy narratives. For example, 450 words across 30 sentences averages 15 words each; with 1.5 syllables per word grade lands 8.0. Shorten 28-word monsters toward grade 7.
  - How is grade level derived?
    - Answer: Formula FKGL equals 0.39 times ASL plus 11.8 times ASW minus 15.59, where ASL means words per sentence plus ASW means syllables per word. For example, 450 words in 30 sentences yields ASL 15; combined with ASW 1.5 grade reaches 8.0. Trim length to descend.
  - Which targets suit general audiences?
  - Is my draft uploaded?
  - Why do lists skew scores?
- Steps: Paste text (Insert 600-word article containing 30 sentences averaging 15 words for assessment.) → View scores (Review Ease 0-100, grade level, syllable averages, plus word totals instantly.) → Find long sentences → Simplify copy

### Typing Speed Test
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/typing-speed-test
- What: WPM & accuracy
- FAQ:
  - How are WPM plus accuracy derived?
    - Answer: WPM equals characters divided by five per minute; accuracy equals correct keystrokes over total times 100. For example, 62 WPM at 97 percent surpasses 40 average; 60 plus signals professional while 80 plus denotes elite. Sixty-second windows balance stamina.

    - Answer: No. Sixty-second timing, WPM arithmetic, plus history persist wholly inside your browser tab sans outward dispatch. Achieve 62 WPM at 97 percent after initial load sans accounts. Inputs evaporate on reset while summaries remain viewable today.

### Base64 Encode / Decode
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/base64-tool
- What: Encode and decode Base64 text
- FAQ:
  - Does Base64 encrypt my data?
    - Answer: No. Base64 merely repackages bytes into readable characters, offering zero confidentiality. Anyone pasting aGVsbG8= instantly recovers Hello, so concealing mango123 as encoded text remains trivially reversible. Treat it as transport armor for email and JSON, never as secrecy. For genuine protection, employ password-based AES at /aes-encryptor with robust keys.
  - Is Unicode text supported?
    - Answer: Yes. Characters first map to UTF-8 bytes, so accents, emoji, and twelve scripts survive round trips. For example, Hello becomes aGVsbG8= with single pad, decoding restores Hello exactly, while a 50KB note with 800 emoji lines converts within a second. All processing stays inside this tab. No upload occurs.
  - Does it support URL-safe Base64?
  - Why does encoded size grow by roughly one third?
- Steps: Paste input (Paste plain wording like Hello or encoded value like aGVsbG8= into the upper field for immediate conversion.) → Choose mode (Choose Encode to transform text outward, Decode for reverse, then toggle URL-safe when building links or tokens.) → Handle Unicode → Copy output

### Hash Generator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/hash-generator
- What: SHA-1 / 256 / 512 of any text
- FAQ:
  - Which hash algorithms can I generate here?
    - Answer: Select SHA-1 with 40 hex characters, SHA-256 with 64, SHA-384 with 96, plus SHA-512 with 128, alongside MD5 solely for legacy verification. For illustration, hello yields SHA-256 starting 2cf24dba within ten milliseconds, while 100KB manuals finish near fifty milliseconds. Uppercase toggle aligns with checksum manifests from vendors.
  - Is hashing the same as encryption?
    - Answer: No. Hashing applies a one-way compression that never restores source, whereas encryption reverses with a secret key. For example, SHA-256 of mango123 appears random and discloses nothing, while AES ciphertext decrypts with Correct-Horse-9. Employ hashes for integrity fingerprints, reserve AES at /aes-encryptor for confidential messages requiring recovery.
  - How do I compare hashes to verify integrity?
  - Why do tiny edits avalanche digests completely?

    - Answer: Yes. It uses crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling for a true 50-50 split of Heads and Tails. For example, 1,000 flips land near 500 Heads with about 16 standard deviation, while 4-in-a-row streaks appear roughly once per 30 tosses. Each result stays local offline with no tracking.
  - Is the flip cryptographically secure?
    - Answer: Yes. Unlike Math.random, it draws from the browser CSPRNG via crypto.getRandomValues with no exposed seed. For example, 10,000 flips converge near 5,000 Heads within about 50 deviation, proving uniformity. Nothing uploads, history clears on tab close, and rerolls stay independent fully offline.

### Random Passphrase
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/random-passphrase
- What: Generate secure passphrase
- FAQ:
  - How is passphrase randomness generated securely?
    - Answer: It uses crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling for unbiased Fisher-Yates shuffling of a 120-word list. For example, orbit-mango-harbor-bright comes from secure picks, not Math.random. All shuffling runs fully locally offline free with no transfer or logging.
  - How strong is a 4-word passphrase?
    - Answer: Entropy is log2 of 120 to the 4th, about 27.6 bits, good for casual logins but low for vaults. For example, bright-harbor-mango-orbit resists casual guessing yet falls to GPUs. Use 6 to 7 words for 41 to 48 bits on important accounts daily.

## Finance & Money

### Mortgage Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/mortgage-calculator
- What: EMI & amortization schedule
- FAQ:
  - How is my monthly mortgage payment calculated?
    - Answer: Your payment comes from EMI = P×r×(1+r)^n÷((1+r)^n−1), where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly rate (annual÷12÷100), and n is months. For example, $240,000 at 6% for 30 years gives r=0.005 and n=360, so EMI lands near $1,439 with lifetime interest near $278,000. Extra principal shortens the term. See /terms.
  - Is this mortgage calculator financial advice?
    - Answer: No. It is an informational home-loan planning tool only, not financial advice. Taxes, insurance, PMI, HOA dues, closing costs, and adjustable-rate resets are excluded from every figure. For example, a $200 monthly escrow adds $2,400 per year on top. Consult your lender for exact numbers and see /terms before applying.

    - Answer: Frequency sets how often interest rejoins principal: yearly uses 1, half-yearly 2, quarterly 4, and monthly 12. More frequent compounding raises maturity slightly at the same rate. For example, Rs 50,000 at 8% for 10 years grows larger with monthly rests than yearly ones. Compare both options in the tool and see /terms.

    - Answer: Take-home pay equals gross salary minus taxes and deductions. First subtract pre-tax items, such as a $5,200 retirement contribution and $3,100 insurance, from $82,000 gross. ### Profit Margin Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/profit-margin-calculator
- What: Calculate margin & markup
- FAQ:
  - What is the difference between margin and markup?
    - Answer: Margin equals profit divided by revenue times 100, while markup equals profit divided by cost times 100. For example, a $60 cost with a $100 price gives $40 profit, a 40% margin, and a 66.7% markup. Margin guides pricing strategy; markup guides cost-plus quotes. Run both figures in the tool and see /terms.
  - Is this profit margin calculator pricing advice?
    - Answer: No. It gives math help only for pricing, never professional pricing advice. Overheads, taxes, shipping, discounts, and refunds are excluded from every result. For example, a 40% margin can vanish after ad spend and fees. Consult your accountant about true costs and see /terms before changing prices.

### Inflation Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/inflation-calculator
- What: Future purchasing power
- FAQ:
  - How do you calculate future value with inflation?
    - Answer: Future cost equals present amount times (1+rate)^years, while purchasing power equals amount divided by (1+rate)^years. For example, $100 at 3% inflation for 10 years grows to $134.39 future cost, so $100 today feels like $74.41 then. Try 2% versus 5% to feel erosion. See /terms.
  - Is this inflation calculator economic advice?
    - Answer: No, this inflation projection is illustrative math only, never economic advice. Official CPI baskets, housing costs, and personal spending differ widely from flat 3% assumptions. Compare 2% versus 5% scenarios over 20 years, then consult a qualified professional and see /terms before budgeting.

### Retirement Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/retirement-calculator
- What: Plan your savings goal
- FAQ:
  - What return should I assume for retirement planning?
    - Answer: Start with 5 to 7% nominal returns minus 2 to 3% inflation for a 3 to 4% real rate. The tool shows both nominal corpus and inflation-adjusted shortfall against your goal. For example, $800 monthly at 7% for 30 years approaches $980,000 nominal but far less in today's dollars. Test conservative rates and see /terms.
  - How is my retirement corpus calculated?
    - Answer: Corpus combines current savings grown as P×(1+r)^t plus monthly contributions as PMT×(((1+mr)^n−1)÷mr), where mr is annual÷12÷100 and n is months. For example, $800 monthly at 7% for 30 years grows near $980,000 before inflation, plus existing savings compounding separately. Real value divides by (1+inflation)^years. See /terms; this is never financial advice.

### CAGR Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/cagr-calculator
- What: Growth rate + multiple
- FAQ:
  - How is CAGR calculated?
    - Answer: CAGR equals (end÷start)^(1÷years)−1, with multiple as end÷start and gain as end−start. For example, $10,000 growing to $20,000 in 5 years gives about 14.87% CAGR, a 2x multiple, and a $10,000 gain. It smooths yearly volatility into one steady rate for comparison. See /terms.

### Debt Payoff Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/debt-payoff-calculator
- What: Snowball vs avalanche
- FAQ:
  - Which saves more: debt snowball or avalanche?
    - Answer: Avalanche attacks the highest APR first and minimizes lifetime interest, while snowball clears the smallest balance first for momentum. Example: $5,000 at 24% minimum $150 plus $2,000 at 18% with $200 extra finishes months sooner under avalanche and saves noticeable interest.
  - How does the debt payoff cascade work?
    - Answer: The simulator pools all minimums plus your extra payment into one fixed monthly amount, then rolls each freed minimum into the next priority debt. Example: $150 plus $80 minimums plus $200 extra creates a $430 pool that cascades automatically until every balance reaches zero.

    - Answer: For FY 2025-26 the tool uses listed-equity LTCG at 12.5% above the Rs 1,25,000 exemption for holdings over 12 months, equity STCG at 20%, and property plus gold LTCG at 12.5%. Shorter property and gold holds join slab rates. Verify the Finance Act notice and see /terms.
  - Is indexation included in this calculation?
    - Answer: No. Purchases after 23 July 2024 use flat 12.5% LTCG without indexation in this simplified estimate. Older property and gold buys may pick 20% with indexation in some notified cases. For example, pre-cutoff buys need deed-date checks. Confirm your purchase date with a CA and see /terms.

  - When should 50-10 replace 25-5?
- Steps: Set times (Configure 25 work minutes, 5 rest minutes, plus four cycles for balanced focus rhythm.) → Start countdown (Launch drift-corrected timer observing progress ring plus round counter advancement.) → Get alert → Finish cycle
